exact_claim: Anthropic and Theorem announced their verification effort on 22 October 2026, one day after the coordinated PHP2Shell disclosure and PHP security release.
evidence: Publisher dates and the PHP Foundation chronology establish the two dates.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Leaks and a pre-announcement occurred on 20 October. Do not call 21 October the first discovery or first public awareness. The chronology does not establish that the verification project was a response to PHP2Shell.

exact_claim: The announcement reports 239 fuzzing entry points across 123 open-source libraries.
evidence: The announcement-wide result is larger than the initial public proof subset.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: These are publisher-reported figures. The 123-library collection was not independently audited here; libraries and executable clients are different counting units.

exact_claim: At the audited initial snapshot, the public inventory contains 25 projects, 60 harnesses, and 138 agreement results: 55 ASan, 34 UBSan, and 49 combined.
evidence: The retained README lists each proved harness/variant pair; the CSV tables reproduce its counts.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Counts are for commit 98e995d4, not current HEAD. Variants are not separate upstream versions, and counts do not measure allocator review depth.

exact_claim: The audit fixes commit 98e995d4 from 23 October 2026, immediately after the initial v2026.10.0 release tag.
evidence: Retained commit metadata gives parent 8f5f46768858af236a4270f9628e6beed9aa0e72 and a CI-only commit message.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Do not call the audit SHA the release tag target. Subsequent release notes have mutable descriptions; their captured metadata is dated in this bundle.

exact_claim: The audited results concern fixed static RISC-V executables and a modeled Linux process, with single-threaded execution and musl builds.
evidence: README, semantics documentation, and the pinned LPS scope specify the executable/model boundary.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: This is not a theorem about arbitrary x86/ARM deployments, dynamic glibc linking, or concurrent clients. RV64G compiler targets and RV64GC model support are separate facts.

exact_claim: The inspected file-input wrappers reject files of 64 MiB or more before invoking the harness; the wrapper format includes a configuration prefix.
evidence: The msgpack and simdjson dossiers record the concrete file-input threshold and driver format in Statements.v. The announcement uses the shorthand 64 MB.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: This bounds accepted file inputs, not all heap usage. The theorem can also cover driver rejections. Do not silently treat the whole file limit as payload length after its header.

exact_claim: Agreement results condition on the plain run staying within its budget; the recorded budgets are 2 GiB for ASan-bearing comparisons and 16 GiB for UBSan-only comparisons, with a 512 GiB target-side budget.
evidence: Shapes.v and prior statement/provenance inspection distinguish source and target budgets. Later release notes say these budget premises have not been discharged for released agreement builds.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Do not infer that every admitted input fits the source budget or that out-of-memory behavior is universally covered. Allocation-failure policies also differ by statement form.

exact_claim: The agreement proposition combines modeled error freedom with equality of observable behavior sets between specified plain and sanitizer binaries.
evidence: The initial README explains both components; Shapes.v instantiates LPS error-free agreement forms. Observations include process I/O, exit status, and modeled file contents.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: It is stronger than merely equal outputs. It still needs a specification/model connection to establish additional logical-object or functional properties.

exact_claim: The initial audited snapshot has no published halts result; later releases add termination proofs.
evidence: Initial README explicitly separates agreement from halts. v2026.10.1 adds 64 halts statements and v2026.10.2 adds two further halts statements.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: A timeless statement that the release has no termination proofs is false after the update. The broader announcement wording about exiting normally must not replace the exact initial public theorem.

exact_claim: Verifying a fixed harness restricts the client program, while the theorem remains universal over its admitted modeled inputs under its premises.
evidence: The README states universal input quantification and executable scope; harness sources identify the actual caller.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Neither finite testing nor verification of every possible library client is an accurate description.

exact_claim: Modeled error freedom and sanitizer agreement do not automatically establish full library functional correctness.
evidence: The corpus README explicitly disclaims library correctness; the reviewed parser harnesses do not provide a general semantic oracle for MessagePack or JSON.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: An individual supporting lemma can still prove a specific functional fact. Do not claim the entire proof corpus contains no functional reasoning.

exact_claim: Anthropic explicitly acknowledges that ASan misses memory-safety errors and that harness coverage and caller behavior limit the claims.
evidence: The main announcement Limitations section states each general boundary. A targeted reread on 29 October confirmed that it does not name custom allocators.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: The main announcement acknowledges ASan incompleteness in general; it does not specifically discuss custom allocators, suballocation boundaries, or internal object lifetimes. The custom-allocator analysis is ours. Do not attribute that specific analysis to Anthropic. This attribution check concerns the main blog post, not every linked document.

exact_claim: Ordinary ASan may track one live backing allocation without recognizing the client subobjects managed inside it.
evidence: The ASan design and CMASan arena/recycler discussion explain standard allocator interception and custom-allocator blind spots.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Manual poisoning, redzones, allocator substitution, and specialized instrumentation can change coverage. Their presence in a particular build must be checked; do not universally say ASan cannot support custom allocators.

exact_claim: After reused storage is unpoisoned, address-only accessibility checks cannot distinguish an expired reference from a newly issued reference with the same address.
direct_or_inferred: inferred from mechanism and stated API contract
evidence: The references have identical observed addresses but distinct stipulated logical allocation identities. The claim follows from what the check observes.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: This is a contract-sensitive illustration. It is not a universal claim about C/C++ transparent replacement, nor evidence that a verified client retains an expired reference.

exact_claim: CMASan reports 19 previously unknown custom-allocator memory bugs that ordinary ASan missed.
evidence: The CMASan abstract and evaluation report this result, including arena/recycler and clear/reuse examples.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: These are CMASan authors results, not bugs discovered by this handoff. Do not transfer their bugs to the audited revisions or binaries.

exact_claim: The 20-category checklist in this bundle is a synthesis for auditing desired guarantees, not an exhaustive specification supplied by CMASan.
evidence: The original dossiers preserve a 17-item supplied checklist and three extensions concerning initialization/residual data, arithmetic/alignment, and races.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: CMASan supports particular allocator failure mechanisms and detector design. Other contracts and C/C++ semantic issues require their own arguments.

exact_claim: A client access should be related to an authorizing logical allocation identity, its current extent, and its liveness at the time of access.
evidence: The paper proposes live(o,t) and containment of the full nonwrapping access interval in the current object interval. The identity must be linked to the reference, not chosen existentially by address.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: This is not an already proved theorem. Use time-dependent bounds for resizing and same-layer separation for distinct client allocations; nested backing/suballocations legitimately overlap.

exact_claim: Final-memory preservation alone does not constrain every intermediate read or write.
evidence: The simdjson dossier identifies munch in Lib/Frame.v as boundary preservation. A read can leave final memory unchanged; a temporary write followed by restoration can also preserve the relation.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: The illustration targets that relation alone. Other invariants and actual control flow may forbid the illustrated access. It is not an extracted binary trace.

exact_claim: Uninstrumented runtime code is not automatically outside the machine-level proof.
evidence: Build documentation identifies sanitizer exclusions, while the proof corpus contains reached runtime instruction reasoning and contracts.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Less instrumentation limits the sanitizer oracle. It does not by itself establish an unchecked assumption about every such function.

exact_claim: Four projects received detailed selected-path proof review: msgpack-c, simdjson, OpenSSL, and pupnp; their project inventories sum to 19 harnesses and 41 agreements.
evidence: The initial README and reports support 1/3, 10/24, 7/12, and 1/2 harness/agreement counts. These four are the detailed-proof subset of the restored twelve-project survey recorded in C051.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: The four-project count measures detailed selected-path proof review, not the full allocator survey. It is neither an exhaustive allocator census nor 41 complete audits. Boost.JSON has a separate pinned source-presence check; seven additional projects retain inherited source/configuration findings with their reported exclusions and corrections.

exact_claim: msgpack-c unpack_pack_fuzzer creates fresh owning state, unpacks with six limits of 1000, packs, catches exceptions, and cleans up local state.
evidence: The harness and original dossier trace the fresh-zone owning overload. There is no comparison of output with input or a semantic oracle.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Driver repetition is not retention of a zone pointer across calls. This is the C++ zone workload even though the repository is named msgpack-c.

exact_claim: msgpack-c explicitly proves allocation fit, alignment, freshness/non-overlap, requested-size regions, and selected array/map bounds.
evidence: Unp/Steps.v supplies zalloc8_fits_ok, zalloc1_fits_ok, zalloc_fresh_ok and separation lemmas; G4.v constructs new_region SZ; G3.v carries NEWSLOT bounds.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: These are positive facts. Preserve hypotheses and the selected compiled paths; do not inflate them into a universal original-allocation theorem.

evidence_label: demonstrated counterexample to a predicate implication; not established globally
exact_claim: The completed-tree predicate tree_wf alone does not encode the original allocation request for every payload.
evidence: Its OStr/OBin case uses in_zone and readability. The original dossier gives a toy chunk-contained range that exceeds a hypothetical earlier smaller request.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: The toy state was not shown reachable, was not proved to satisfy all combined invariants, and was not kernel-checked as a countermodel. Stronger construction facts may exclude it.

exact_claim: msgpack zones support clear in the library, but clear-then-retained-use is outside this harness; output sbuffer uses standard realloc separately.
evidence: cpp11_zone.hpp retains one chunk and resets the bump cursor on clear; sbuffer.hpp expands with standard realloc. The reviewed harness does not perform the clear/reuse sequence.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Do not say msgpack has no clear or no realloc. Do not attribute a per-zone-object moving/shrinking realloc API to this workload.

exact_claim: The msgpack proof exports three strong_universal_error_free_unpack_pack_fuzzer theorem instances for ASan, UBSan, and both.
evidence: Theorems.v records suffixes _asan, _ubsan, and _both and instantiates strong_universal_error_free_T_scfg_budgets_abort.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Symbols are preserved from the prior dossier; this handoff did not run Rocq. These are not source-language MessagePack correctness theorems.

exact_claim: The initial simdjson inventory has ten proved harnesses and 24 agreements: nine ASan, eight UBSan, and seven combined.
evidence: The inventory and original dossier list exact variants. There are 13 buildable harnesses with statements, not 13 proved harnesses.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: One upstream revision plus a recorded patch underlies the variants. Do not call 24 results 24 versions; fuzz_dump has no combined agreement in this snapshot.

exact_claim: simdjson DOM proofs track individual string-record extents, lengths, headers, terminators, and sequential layout within the used prefix.
evidence: SjTape.v str_at requires o+l+5<=sn and represents length and terminator. SjTapeTile.v str_rec, tilesS, and tape_wfS thread successive records.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Scoped to the identified proof paths. An ASan blind spot does not erase this stronger internal reasoning.

exact_claim: The On-Demand decoder contracts include a bounded output cursor and a permitted output footprint, with variant-specific proof connections.
evidence: Od_pstr_kit.v pstr_post_g bounds sbo<=sbo_prime<=sbo+(j-i-1); pstr_spec and ASan-bearing pstra_spec/pstrb_spec connect compiled decoder variants in the original dossier.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: The eventual view extent and decoder scratch/output permission differ. The footprint relation alone is not an all-intermediate-access theorem.

exact_claim: The reviewed simdjson clients do not retain a view across a later parse on the same parser; the documented DOM API invalidates views on reparse/destruction.
evidence: The original dossier enumerates the ten proved client sequences and upstream DOM element documentation.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: An illustrative stale-view client violates an API contract and is not a demonstrated vulnerability in the verified harness. Exact consequences of every On-Demand rewind remain unresolved.

exact_claim: Individual string free, wrong-pool free, and per-string realloc are not operations of the simdjson arenas inspected here.
evidence: The source descriptions and dossier matrix identify append-style string storage and bulk invalidation/backing-buffer replacement.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Do not mark an operation absent from the interface as a failed safety guarantee. Backing allocations and parser reuse still have lifetime obligations.

exact_claim: The inspected simdjson layout/decoder contracts do not by themselves specify the complete decoded JSON value.
evidence: The dossier separates bounded record layout and pstr_post_g from equality between decoded bytes and a JSON semantic specification.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: This does not say every functional fact is absent from the corpus. A bounded-but-wrong illustrative payload is not an observed parser output.

exact_claim: OpenSSL has seven proved harnesses and twelve agreement results in the initial snapshot; detailed allocator reasoning here concerns bndiv and bignum.
evidence: The inventory lists bignum, bndiv, ct, echconfiglist_parser, hashtable, pem, and punycode. The original dossier records its selected paths.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Seven harnesses does not mean seven BN_CTX audits. Full binary hashes and exact top-level theorem symbols for every variant were not all recorded.

exact_claim: BN_CTX_end expires temporary-pointer API leases while retaining pool backing storage for reuse.
evidence: Pinned documentation states the invalidation rule; bn_ctx.c restores usage/frame state without freeing every backing pool item.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: This is logical/API invalidation, not necessarily the end of the underlying C allocation lifetime. Ordinary BN_free and digit-buffer frees are separate.

evidence_label: supporting proof definition; analytical contract counterexample
exact_claim: In bndiv, valid_ref for RPool i requires i<3 and a nonempty pool; that predicate can remain true after modeled frame-end expires the lease.
evidence: BnInv.v:45-46 defines valid_ref. BnModel.v:368-380 retains cx_vals at BN_CTX_end. BnSpecs.v:416-420 requires valid_ref in the setter specification without an active-lease premise.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: This tests predicate adequacy, not reachability in the verified binary. The original dossier also discusses valid_refm, based on retained length; do not merge the definitions.

exact_claim: OpenSSL bignum has explicit liveness guards and preservation of temporaries in still-active outer frames.
direct_or_inferred: direct liveness definition; inherited guard and callsite review
evidence: BgInv.v live(r,s) is r<NFIX+gx_used(st_ctx s); BgArith uses bn_live. The earlier temporal audit traced frame-owning model callsites and records no escaped post-end use.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Current-slot liveness is not a universal original-generation theorem. Missing generations alone does not establish an unsafe client.

exact_claim: Selected OpenSSL instruction proofs establish concrete limb, copy, conversion, and expansion bounds.
evidence: The original dossier names AW_mul_words, W_copyAF, W_bin2bnA, and W_expandAF and explains loop ranges, owned arrays, exact copy lengths, and allocate/copy/free.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: The dossier retains the leaf module names; their complete repository paths were not re-established for this handoff. The repository directory links are navigation only; the recovered original dossier is the direct retained evidence. Snapshots of every named leaf are not included. Selected positive facts are not an all-instruction access certificate.

exact_claim: The recorded OpenSSL pem proof fixes the secure heap to its disabled state and follows ordinary allocation fallback.
evidence: The original OpenSSL dossier explicitly identifies this configuration exclusion.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Do not claim the secure buddy allocator was verified. Exact exclusion symbol/path is an open provenance detail if expanded into a major blog claim. The repository directory links are navigation only; the recovered original dossier is the direct retained evidence.

exact_claim: pupnp FuzzHttp has ASan and combined agreement results, and its reviewed client initializes an HTTP parser, appends one input, and destroys the message.
evidence: Initial README lists two variants; the pinned harness and FreeList source are included among selected snapshots.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: No standalone UBSan agreement is published for this harness in the initial snapshot. General arbitrary allocator histories are not the harness.

exact_claim: pupnp proofs distinguish backing blocks from cached nodes and exclude duplicate cached returns under their premises.
evidence: FreeListFree_post_A retains LB when caching and extends FB; it uses NoDup(map blk_id FB_prime). FreeListFree_stmt_A requires uniqueness including the returned node. Destroy removes owned blocks.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: This contradicts a blanket claim that internal release or cleanup is ignored. The invariant is scoped to the modeled client and preconditions.

exact_claim: The pupnp allocation lemma inspected in plain, ASan, and combined proofs assumes an empty freelist cache.
evidence: FreeListAlloc_stmt_A requires fl_cells 0 fk and invokes malloc for 24 bytes. The P0 and B0 variants have matching empty-head premises.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: It does not establish a reused-node generation-sensitive guarantee. This is not evidence that a stale-node access occurs in FuzzHttp.

evidence_label: source presence only; inherited supplementary finding
exact_claim: Boost.JSON contains a monotonic resource in the pinned source, but its exercise in the verified fuzz_parse configuration was not established.
evidence: The checked monotonic_resource.ipp advances a cursor within backing blocks; do_deallocate is empty and release frees backing blocks. The checked harness calls default parse(sv,ec). Separately, the recovered prior survey (SRC13; source-snapshots/prior-conversations/README.md) identifies value_stack temporary storage; its source-to-compiled-proof chain was not re-established here.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: The directly checked monotonic resource supports a fifth source-presence case, not a fifth detailed proof audit or a claim that this optional resource is exercised. The default parse call does not prove absence of all internal allocation. Keep the inherited value_stack finding separate from the pinned-source check. Superproject and submodule commits differ.

These are richer prior findings than a list of speculative names.

Retention of a prior finding is not a fresh pinned-source verification or Rocq audit; absence of rechecking is also not evidence that the prior identification was refuted. qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: PHP2Shell is context, not a counterexample to a proved PHP result. The inherited six-harness/42-statement details are not a newly rechecked PHP allocator audit.

evidence: Captured v2026.10.1 notes distinguish the modeled stack window from Linux accounting and identify affected results.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Maintainers report no known input forcing the relevant stack usage. This is separate from the allocator argument and is not a demonstrated actual crash.

exact_claim: Updated initial release notes discuss model-layout/allocation-refusal limitations that can exclude inputs or hide output differences in constructed examples.
evidence: The retained notes distinguish constructed examples from released fuzz targets.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Do not transfer a model toy example to a real verified project. It is independent of the custom-allocator predicate observations.

exact_claim: This investigation did not independently replay Rocq proofs, rebuild or execute release binaries, or produce an actual violating binary trace.
evidence: All three original dossiers record source/specification review; the new reports consolidate that method and selected source rechecks.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Compiling and visually checking the LaTeX paper is document QA, not proof-corpus validation. Published proof status remains publisher status.

exact_claim: A universal theorem connecting every relevant machine access to its authorizing original logical object and live lease has not been established by this review.
evidence: The exported proposition, weaker reusable predicates, positive local invariants, and excluded histories are documented separately in the four reports.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: This is not proof that no such theorem follows from the full development. The strongest open task is to derive or refute the explicit property with complete evidence.

exact_claim: None of the four project audits demonstrates a reachable custom-allocation memory-safety violation in the exact verified binary.
evidence: Reports and complete dossiers distinguish hypothetical API misuse, predicate-level examples, and actual program reachability.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Do not use exploit or failure graphics that imply a vulnerability was reproduced. Literature bugs and later model disclosures have different subjects.

exact_claim: Logical invalidation by a custom allocator is not automatically identical to ending a C-language allocation lifetime.
evidence: Backing allocation can remain live while the allocator contract expires client permission, as in the BN_CTX source and API.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: State the intended object model and reference/lease semantics. Do not describe every custom lifetime violation as a demonstrated ISO C/C++ lifetime violation.

exact_claim: Backing-allocation ownership and cleanup evidence do not by themselves establish universal leak freedom, initialization, or confidentiality guarantees.
evidence: The original dossiers distinguish cleanup sequences, subset-based live-block predicates, disabled leak detection, and general definedness or zeroization properties.
qualifications_and_unresolved_questions: Retained arena capacity can be intentional. Do not call every retained byte a leak or every uninitialized capacity byte a client memory-safety error.

exact_claim: PHP CVE-2015-2787 has published arbitrary-code-execution exploit evidence and a separately reported ASan false negative with the allocator shim disabled.

evidence: CMASan Table 4 and section 5.5 list this PHP UAF as missed by ASan with the allocator shim disabled. HushVac Table I and section VI.G evaluate a public arbitrary-code-execution PoC for the same CVE on PHP 5.5.14. PHP security report 68976 explains the lifetime error.
